clue.text: Live on edge

parts.note: RE means on or concerning, as in a letter heading
a side is an edge or border

explanation.surface: An instruction to dwell on the brink of something, living dangerously.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere is to dwell or have your home there, a synonym of live.

clue.text: Reportedly coarse fish

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

parts.note: coarse means rough, and the fish name is pronounced the same

explanation.surface: Anglers call some fish coarse fish, so this reads like a report about angling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coarse fish' is an angling term for freshwater fish other than salmon and trout, which makes the phrase look like one unit.
explanation.definitionFit: The ruff (or ruffe) is a small freshwater fish of the perch family.

clue.text: Mostly abstain from using bar

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to spare something is to refrain from using it

explanation.surface: Advice to a drinker to keep mostly away from the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a pub to avoid, but it is the definition, a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A spar is a stout pole or rod, such as a mast or boom on a ship.

clue.text: One may be found in a bar surrounded by doubles

definitions.text: One may be found in a bar surrounded by doubles

parts.words: One may be found in a bar surrounded by doubles
parts.note: surface reading: a drinker in a pub surrounded by double measures of spirits
setter's reading: a pub game target whose outer ring is the doubles band

explanation.surface: Someone propping up the bar surrounded by double whiskies.
explanation.walkthrough: The outer narrow ring of the pub game's target scores double, so the doubles really do surround it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dartboard hangs in many pubs, and its scoring area is ringed by the doubles band.

clue.text: Mine leaders, intellectuals

parts.note: egg is old military slang for a mine or bomb
heads are leaders or chiefs

explanation.surface: Mining bosses who are also the brainy sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mine leaders' looks like a single phrase about colliery managers; split it into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Egghead is an informal, often mocking word for a highbrow or academic person.

clue.text: Gathers bottles to blow? They may provide the music

indicators.note: to blow something up is to wreck it, so these letters are scattered and rebuilt

parts.note: the fourteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone collects bottles to blow across their necks for a tune.
explanation.walkthrough: Blowing over bottles does make music, so the surface hangs together while hiding the mechanism.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghetto blasters are large portable stereos, so they supply the music at a gathering.

clue.text: Building hospital overlooking river

indicators.note: in a down entry, something overlooking another sits above it, so the first part comes on top

parts.note: H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital
the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: A hospital built with a view over the river.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'overlooking' means placed above, so the hospital letter sits on top of the river. The Ouse flows through York.
explanation.definitionFit: A house is a dwelling, one kind of building.

clue.text: Reluctant to mix in Calais? Not I, surprisingly

indicators.note: a surprising outcome is unexpected, so these letters come out in an unexpected order

parts.note: the ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A shy traveller denies being the one who wouldn't mingle in Calais.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mix' looks like an anagram signal but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone antisocial avoids the company of others, unwilling to socialise.

clue.text: Season then toss a Chinese pancake

parts.note: spring is one of the four seasons
to roll dice is to toss them

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: add seasoning, then toss the pancake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Season' and 'toss' read as kitchen verbs; here they are a time of year and a throw.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring roll is a thin pancake wrapper rolled round a filling and fried, a Chinese dish.

clue.text: They may take in what's been said

definitions.text: They may take in what's been said

parts.words: They may take in what's been said
parts.note: surface reading: listeners or note-takers absorbing a speech
setter's reading: punctuation marks that literally enclose quoted speech

explanation.surface: Attentive people absorbing what a speaker says.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take in' suggests understanding; here it means physically enclose, as quotation marks do around speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Quotation marks are placed either side of reported speech, enclosing the words spoken.

clue.text: Country importing a Greek perfume

indicators.note: importing means bringing goods within the borders, so one part goes inside the other

parts.note: a country in Europe
taken as written
GR is the abbreviation for Greek

explanation.surface: France buying in a scent from Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragrance is a pleasant smell, and also a name for a scent or perfume product.

clue.text: Golf club lacking power, say

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: a putter is the club used on the green
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: A golfer's weak putt blamed on the club, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like an aside meaning 'for example' but it is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter something is to speak it aloud, a synonym of say.

clue.text: Don't protest as much about a punishment intended as a warning to others?

definitions.text: a punishment intended as a warning to others

parts.note: to protest is to object, and not doing it as much is objecting less
on means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A plea not to complain so much about a deterrent penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the instruction literally: object less on (about) something.
explanation.definitionFit: An object lesson is a practical example teaching a moral, often a punishment meant to deter others.

clue.text: End with bull in game

parts.note: the back is the rear end of something
gammon is old slang for nonsense, as is bull

explanation.surface: A bullfight or game where the bull finally ends up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bull' here means nonsense, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Backgammon is a board game for two played with dice and counters.

clue.text: Capone inside cut open a fresh musk melon

indicators.note: inside places one part within the other
fresh means new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: the eight letters to be rearranged
Al Capone was the Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: Al Capone slicing open a fresh melon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut open' looks like a kitchen action but provides letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The cantaloupe is a variety of musk melon with orange flesh and ribbed skin.

clue.text: Completely determined woman, married social worker

parts.note: Ada is a woman's name
M is the abbreviation for married
the ant is a social insect and a worker

explanation.surface: A resolute married woman employed in social work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' is a profession in the surface; in crosswords it often means an insect living in colonies.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant means utterly unyielding and refusing to change one's mind.

clue.text: Doorman, extremely bitter, carrying little weight

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within, so one part goes inside
extremely points to the extremes, the first and last letters of the word

parts.note: the end letters of the word
an ounce is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: A bitter doorman who doesn't throw his weight around.
explanation.definitionFit: A bouncer is employed at a club door to keep out or eject troublemakers.

clue.text: Guild to raise flag

parts.note: a guild is an association, a union
to jack up is to raise

explanation.surface: A trade guild deciding to hoist its banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise flag' reads as one action; split it so 'flag' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Union Jack is the national flag of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: Coolidge's girl carried out an insect

parts.note: Katy is the heroine of Susan Coolidge's children's novel What Katy Did
did means performed or carried out

explanation.surface: A girl from a Coolidge book catching and removing a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: Coolidge suggests the US president, but it is Susan Coolidge, whose 'What Katy Did' sits inside the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The katydid is a North American bush cricket, named for its call.

clue.text: Serving girl may cause a grown-up trouble

parts.note: taken as written
big means grown-up, as children say
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A maid making difficulties for an adult.
explanation.definitionFit: Abigail is a dated word for a lady's maid, from a character in a 17th-century play.

clue.text: Patrolman lit flares identified as essential

indicators.note: something that flares bursts out wildly, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the twelve letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A police officer lights emergency flares deemed vital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flares' looks like a noun, the things lit; it is a verb signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Something all-important is vital and of the greatest significance, so essential.

clue.text: Encountered aluminium and copper, say

parts.note: met means encountered
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: A list of metals someone came across: aluminium and copper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' could be a police officer, but 'say' marks it as an example of the category.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper is an example of a metal, which 'say' signals as one of a class.

clue.text: One female in car shows flair

indicators.note: in places these letters within the car abbreviation

parts.note: GT, gran turismo, is a type of sports car
I is the Roman numeral one
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A woman driving a sports car with style.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift is a natural talent or aptitude, which is what flair means.

clue.text: Spots rook over wood

parts.note: R is the chess notation for rook
ash is a type of wood

explanation.surface: Someone spots a rook flying over the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spots' looks like a verb, seeing a bird; it is a noun for an outbreak on the skin. In a down entry 'over' puts the rook letter on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash is an outbreak of red spots or patches on the skin.

clue.text: Horse seen from hill

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an animal one rides
second meaning: a mountain, as in a place name

explanation.surface: A horse spotted from the top of a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A mount is a horse for riding, and also a mountain or hill, as in Mount Etna.

clue.text: Cocktail — a small measure knocked over by girl

indicators.note: something knocked over is upended, so the letters are read in the opposite order

parts.note: taken as written
a gram is a small unit of mass
Rita is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl spills a drink, knocking over a tot of a cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small measure' suggests a tot of spirits; here it is a metric unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A margarita is a cocktail of tequila, orange liqueur and lime juice.

clue.text: Unnecessary anger shown on steamship

parts.note: needle means irritation or hostility
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: Pointless rage displayed aboard a steamer.
explanation.definitionFit: Needless means not required, so something unnecessary.

clue.text: Outline of second sailing boat

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: The profile of a second yacht in a fleet.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketch is a rough drawing or brief outline of something.
